definition: The 81 hardships are not mere calamities but 81 kinds of mind-nature trials, corresponding to the mind-cultivation sequence of the Duoxin Jing

representative_hardships: Four Sages Test the Mind of Chan
Stealing the Ginseng Fruit at Wuzhuang
allegory_categories.buddhist_counterpart: the poison of greed, foremost of the Three Poisons

representative_hardships: Thrice Beating the White Bone Demon
allegory_categories.buddhist_counterpart: the poison of anger, second of the Three Poisons
the poison of ignorance, third of the Three Poisons

representative_hardships: Green Ox Spirit of Jindou Mountain
allegory_categories.buddhist_counterpart: pride, one of the Five Hindrances

representative_hardships: Wukong expelled after thrice beating the White Bone Demon
Yellow-Robed Monster returns to Flower-Fruit Mountain
allegory_categories.buddhist_counterpart: doubt, one of the Five Hindrances
sensual desire, one of the Five Desires
birth and death are the great matter

allegory_summary.most_frequent_test: Anger Test (15 times), corresponding to Wukong's primary mind-nature
allegory_summary.least_frequent_test: Fame Test (7 times), corresponding to the pilgrimage team's already-detached disposition
core_findings: The 'count' of the 81 hardships corresponds to the 'eighty-one aspects' of the Duoxin Jing
Wukong's primary practice is anger (15 hardships), Bajie's primary practice is lust (11 hardships)
Tang Sanzang's primary practice is ignorance (10 hardships), often deceived through not seeing the truth
The whole book is a cultivation allegory of 'taming the mind-monkey and thought-horse', not a simple adventure story

heart_sutra_connection.sutra_chapter: Ch. 19, taught by Wuchao Chan Master
heart_sutra_connection.sutra_role: The Heart Sutra is the pilgrimage team's 'guiding thought'; Tang Sanzang recites it daily
heart_sutra_connection.allegory_pattern: The Heart Sutra teaches 'emptiness', the 81 hardships teach 'breaking attachment'; the two correspond
heart_sutra_connection.key_quote: Form is not different from emptiness, emptiness is not different from form; form is emptiness, emptiness is form
heart_sutra_connection.allegory_meaning: Breaking attachment to form (external things) and returning to emptiness (the true mind)
